mstts:express-as.prosody:
As we wrap up, just take a moment to recognize how far you’ve come. If you’re still listening, you already know—talking about race isn’t a one-time thing, or some box you check and forget. It’s a lifelong journey. Sure, it can get messy, and yeah, it’s often uncomfortable... but that’s what makes it matter.
It’s not about getting everything right—it’s about moving forward, one step at a time. Every conversation, every pause to reflect, every time you listen instead of jumping in... they all add up to something real. It’s how we get closer to a world where everyone feels seen, heard, and valued.
So, here are a few reminders you can carry with you:
Listening—truly listening—is way more powerful than always having the perfect words. Mistakes? They’re going to happen. What matters is owning them and choosing to grow. Remember, being an ally isn’t a title, it’s a practice. It’s about showing up, learning, and acting—over and over again.
And no one should have to speak for everyone else. Every story is unique, and every person deserves to be honored for who they are. Real change? It’s built on small, steady actions, not flashy gestures or quick fixes.
As you keep going, know you’re not alone in this work. That discomfort you feel? It means you’re stretching. The conversations you start, the honest questions you ask, the support you give—these things matter, even if it doesn’t always feel like it.
You’re going to face doubt, maybe even feel worn out sometimes. But you’ll also find moments of connection, understanding, and hope. So keep showing up—for yourself, and for others. The world you want to see gets built one conversation, one relationship, and one act of courage at a time.
Trust that what you’re doing—even if it’s imperfect—is part of something bigger. Keep going. You’re making more of a difference than you know.
